articles.title: DyMT-ESB: Dynamic Multi-Turn Evaluation of Social Bias in User-LLM Interactions
articles.zh: DyMT-ESB：用户与LLM交互中社会偏见的多轮动态评估
articles.summary: 如果你在做AI安全或合规方向的内容，这套多轮动态评测值得知道——单轮提问测不出对话里真正冒出来的偏见
articles.author: Rem Hida, Masahiro Kaneko 等
articles.body: Warning: This paper contains examples of stereotypes and social bias. LLMs are increasingly used in interactive settings by the general public, making the evaluation of model behavior in multi-turn conversational scenarios important for safety, including stereotyping-related harms. However, existing multi-turn social bias evaluations often rely on pre-specified or template-based user inputs that do not adapt to model responses and typically assume a fixed dialogue length in advance. In this paper, we study social bias dynamics in response-conditioned multi-turn interactions using a controlled evaluation protocol that generates follow-up user queries from the evolving dialogue history and allows evaluation over variable numbers of turns. Experimental results show that LLMs exhibit social bias even in coherent, response-conditioned multi-turn interactions, revealing late-emerging bias, non-monotonic bias patterns, and bias re-emergence. These results motivate evaluations that extend beyond fixed-turn, pre-scripted protocols. Our findings highlight the importance of analyzing social bias as a turn-level dynamic phenomenon.
articles.bodyZh: 警告：本论文包含刻板印象和社会偏见示例。大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被公众用于互动场景，因此评估模型在多轮对话情境中的行为对于安全至关重要，包括与刻板印象相关的危害。然而，现有的多轮社会偏见评估往往依赖于预先指定或基于模板的用户输入，这些输入无法根据模型回应进行调整，并且通常事先假定固定的对话长度。在本文中，我们通过一种受控评估方案研究了以回应为条件的多轮互动中的社会偏见动态，该方案会根据不断演变的对话历史生成后续用户查询，并允许在不同轮数下进行评估。实验结果表明，即使在连贯的、以回应为条件的多轮互动中，大语言模型也会表现出社会偏见，揭示出偏见延迟出现、非单调的偏见模式以及偏见重新出现等现象。这些结果促使我们开展超越固定轮数、预先设定流程的评估。我们的发现凸显了将社会偏见作为轮层级动态现象加以分析的重要性。

articles.title: Fallacy Benchmarks Measure Scheme Recognition, Not Fallacy Detection
articles.zh: 谬误基准测试衡量的是谬误模式识别，而非谬误检测
articles.summary: 如果你打算拿现成的fallacy benchmark证明模型"会逻辑推理"，这篇会告诉你它测的其实只是认不认得出套路
articles.author: Navyansh Singh, Animesh Pathak 等
articles.body: Fallacy-detection benchmarks pair fallacy classes with a single "valid" or "none" class that takes everything data collection did not label as a fallacy. This construction is misleading: a classifier can learn cues that do well on this class without learning to tell a fallacy from a correct argument. We show that the low false-positive rates benchmarks report are an artifact of how the class is built, not evidence of detection ability. The most informative negative for a fallacy is a correct argument using the same argumentation scheme, and such arguments are at most a few percent of the valid class across the four benchmarks we examined. Evaluated on constructed scheme-matched negatives, false-positive rates rise from 16.6% to 58.9% on CoCoLoFa and from 5.7% to 62.0% on Reddit. That rate depends on how the negatives are written, so we also compare two conditions from the same pipeline that differ only in scheme identity. Classifiers label scheme-matched negatives as the source fallacy type 40.9 points more often than wrong-scheme negatives, which are instead identified as the scheme they actually use 85.9% of the time against 0.4% for the source type. The classifier has learned which scheme an argument uses, not whether it uses it correctly, and on the benchmarks' own test sets the two are indistinguishable. The same dissociation appears in three zero-shot LLM detectors that never saw these benchmarks, and the measurement is far lower on a negative class that was built deliberately. We release the items as Scheme Foils. A reported false-positive rate should not be trusted as a measure of detection until the valid class has been audited for scheme-matched coverage.
articles.bodyZh: 谬误检测基准（fallacy-detection benchmarks）通常会把各种谬误类别（fallacy classes）跟单独一个“有效”（valid）或“无”（none）类配在一起；但凡数据收集时没标成谬误的，全塞进这一类。这么搭其实很误导人：分类器（classifier）完全可以学到一些在这类上表现很好的线索，却根本没学会区分“这是谬误”和“这是正确论证”。我们想说明，基准报告里那些很低的假阳性率（false-positive rates），其实是这个类别怎么造出来的副产品，不是它真有检测能力的证据。对识别一个谬误来说，最有信息量的负例（negative），是用了同一套论证方案（argumentation scheme）的正确论证；可我们检查的四个基准里，这类论证最多只占有效类（valid class）的百分之几。换成我们构造的、方案匹配的负例（scheme-matched negatives）来评估，假阳性率在 CoCoLoFa 上从 16.6% 升到 58.9%，在 Reddit 上从 5.7% 升到 62.0%。这个比例还取决于负例是怎么写的，所以我们又比较了同一条流程下的两种情况，它们唯一的差别就是方案身份（scheme identity）。分类器把方案匹配的负例标成源谬误类型（source fallacy type）的比例，比方案不匹配的负例（wrong-scheme negatives）高出 40.9 个百分点；而方案不匹配的负例反而有 85.9% 被认成它们实际用的方案，只有 0.4% 被认成源类型。也就是说，分类器学到的是“这段论证用了哪个方案”，而不是“它有没有用对”；而在基准自己的测试集里，这两件事根本分不开。同样的分离现象（dissociation）也出现在三个从没见过这些基准的零样本大语言模型（LLM）检测器（zero-shot LLM detectors）身上；而在一个刻意构建的负例类上，这个测量值会低得多。我们把这些条目作为 Scheme Foils 发布。以后要是没审查有效类里的方案匹配覆盖率（scheme-matched coverage），就别把报告出来的假阳性率当成检测能力的衡量标准。

articles.title: STRETCH the Boundaries: A Unified Self-Taught Framework for Progressive LLM Evolution
articles.zh: STRETCH the Boundaries：面向LLM渐进式演化的统一自学习框架
articles.summary: 如果你关心模型怎么靠自己越练越强，这个自训练+渐进演化的统一框架可以当技术底层素材囤着
articles.author: Yajie Yu, Mark Lee 等
articles.body: Large language models (LLMs) often suffer from capability stagnation in self-improvement training because fixed difficulty levels fail to adapt to their evolving proficiency. To address this issue, we propose STRETCH (Self-Taught Reasoning Evolution via Targeted CHallenge), a unified framework inspired by cognitive scaffolding theory. STRETCH introduces a dynamic Stretch Zone mechanism that continuously aligns question difficulty with the model's solving capability. Within a single parameter space, the model alternates between a Scaffolder that generates adaptive, boundary-pushing challenges and a Learner that that optimizes its solving trajectories through reinforcement learning. This dual-loop co-evolution effectively stabilizes training, mitigates reward hacking and promote progressive reasoning growth. Experiments on both negotiation and operation research benchmarks demonstrate that STRETCH consistently outperforms strong prompting and domain-specific baselines. Further scaffolder configuration analysis shows that dynamic difficulty alignment is critical for sustained capability improvement and synchronized reasoning evolution.
articles.bodyZh: 大型语言模型（Large Language Models, LLMs）在自我提升训练里经常卡在一个问题上：能力涨着涨着就不动了，因为题目难度一直固定不变，跟不上模型不断进化的水平。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了 STRETCH（Self-Taught Reasoning Evolution via Targeted CHallenge，通过定向挑战实现自我教学推理演化），这是一个受认知脚手架理论（cognitive scaffolding theory）启发的统一框架。STRETCH 引入了一个动态“拉伸区”（Stretch Zone）机制，持续让题目难度和模型的解题能力匹配起来。在同一个参数空间里，模型会在两个角色之间来回切换：一个是脚手架生成器（Scaffolder），负责生成自适应的、能把能力边界往外推的挑战；另一个是学习者（Learner），通过强化学习（reinforcement learning）不断优化自己的解题轨迹。这种双循环协同演化（dual-loop co-evolution）能有效稳定训练、减少奖励劫持（reward hacking），并推动推理能力一步步成长。在谈判和运筹学（operations research）基准测试（benchmarks）上的实验都表明，STRETCH 始终优于强大的提示方法（prompting）和特定领域基线（baselines）。对脚手架生成器配置的进一步分析还显示，动态难度对齐对于持续提升能力和让推理同步演化来说，非常关键。

articles.title: CoRe-MARL: Cooperative Redistribution Under Unknown Dynamics Using Recurrent Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
articles.zh: CoRe-MARL：未知动力学下基于循环多智能体强化学习的协作式再分配
articles.summary: 如果你在做多智能体仿真或机器人协同，这篇解决的是环境规则未知时怎么分配任务和收益
articles.author: Naimur Rahman Chowdhury, Shatabdi Sen Prapti 等
articles.body: Emergency management assistance programs, such as relief distribution, are essential for delivering necessary supplies to affected communities. However, these programs operate in a decentralized network of local centers that face uncertain local demand and supply dynamics, resulting in inconsistent avail- ability of local services. Redistribution of supplies among these local centers reduces these imbalances, but the centers often make decisions independently, with limited information and disrupted transportation. This study develops CoRe-MARL, a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework, by formulating a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP). We treat each center as an agent that learns a redistribution policy to improve the service in the worst-case region and reduce the service gap across regions while protecting network-wide service. We incorporate a recurrent network that captures evolving supply and demand dynamics without direct observation, while multi-agent proximal policy optimization (MAPPO) enables centralized training and decentralized execution (CTDE). We evaluate the framework in a simulated environment with diverse trajectories, where exact dynamics are not observed by actors and the MAPPO critic. We compare the recurrent MAPPO with the recurrent independent PPO (IPPO) and a local only heuristic, and find that MAPPO reduces the service gap across local centers and enhances service for the worst-served center while maintaining competitive network-wide service. The recurrent MAPPO also shows consistent performance across diverse trajectory patterns, demonstrating its ability to adapt to evolving dynamics. The findings demonstrate the capability of cooperative learning for decentralized redistribution and improving equitable service under uncertain and evolving dynamics.
articles.bodyZh: 像救灾物资发放（relief distribution）这样的应急管理援助项目（Emergency management assistance programs），说白了，就是把必需的物资送到受灾社区手里的关键手段。可这类项目通常是由一个个地方中心组成的去中心化网络（decentralized network）在运转，各地的需求和供应情况都不确定，结果就是当地服务时有时无、很不稳定。把这些物资在地方中心之间重新调配（redistribution）能缓解这种不平衡，但这些中心往往各做各的决定，信息有限，交通还可能被打断。这项研究提出了 CoRe-MARL，一个合作式多智能体强化学习（cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning, MARL）框架，做法是把它建模成一个去中心化部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程（decentralized partially observable Markov decision process, Dec-POMDP）。我们把每个中心都看成一个智能体（agent），让它学着制定再调配策略（redistribution policy），目标是改善最糟情况地区（worst-case region）的服务，缩小各地区之间的服务差距（service gap），同时不牺牲整个网络的服务水平（network-wide service）。我们还加入了一个循环神经网络（recurrent network），让它在没法直接观测的情况下，也能捕捉不断变化的供需动态；同时用多智能体近端策略优化（multi-agent proximal policy optimization, MAPPO）来实现集中训练、分散执行（centralized training and decentralized execution, CTDE）。我们在一个仿真环境（simulated environment）里评估这个框架，里面有很多不同的轨迹（trajectories），而且动作网络（actor）和 MAPPO 的评论网络（critic）都看不到真实动态（exact dynamics）。我们把这种循环 MAPPO 和循环独立 PPO（recurrent independent PPO, IPPO），以及一个只看本地的启发式方法（local only heuristic）做了对比。结果发现，MAPPO 能缩小各地中心之间的服务差距，提升服务最差的中心（worst-served center）的服务，同时全网服务也保持在不输别人的水平。而且，循环 MAPPO 在各种不同轨迹模式下表现都很稳定，说明它有能力适应不断变化的动态。这些发现说明，在不确定、不断变化的情况下，合作学习（cooperative learning）可以用来做去中心化的物资再调配，也能帮助提升更公平的服务（equitable service）。

articles.title: GenStream: Semantic Streaming Framework for Generative Reconstruction of Human-centric Media
articles.zh: GenStream：面向以人为中心的媒体生成式重建的语义流式框架
articles.summary: 如果你关注数字人或实时视频生成，这个流式语义框架是"边推流边重建"路线的一个代表
articles.author: Emanuele Artioli, Daniele Lorenzi 等
articles.body: Video streaming dominates global internet traffic, yet conventional pipelines remain inefficient for structured, human-centric content such as sports, performance, or interactive media. Standard codecs re-encode entire frames, foreground and background alike, treating all pixels uniformly and ignoring the semantic structure of the scene. This leads to significant bandwidth waste, particularly in scenarios where backgrounds are static and motion is constrained to a few salient actors. We introduce GenStream, a semantic streaming framework that replaces dense video frames with compact, structured metadata. Instead of transmitting pixels, GenStream encodes each scene as a combination of skeletal keypoints, camera viewpoint parameters, and a static 3D background model. These elements are transmitted to the client, where a generative model reconstructs photorealistic human figures and composites them into the 3D scene from the original viewpoint. This paradigm enables extreme compression, achieving over 99.9% bandwidth reduction compared to HEVC for the continuous data stream. We partially validate GenStream on Olympic figure skating footage and demonstrate potential for high perceptual fidelity under minimal data. While acknowledging the significant computational costs shifted to the client and challenges in generalization, GenStream opens new directions in volumetric avatar synthesis, canonical 3D actor fusion across views, and personalized viewing experiences, laying the groundwork for scalable, intelligent streaming in the post-codec era.
articles.bodyZh: 视频流媒体（video streaming）撑起了全球互联网流量的绝对大头，可传统那套处理流程（conventional pipelines）碰上体育、表演、互动媒体这种有结构、以人为主的内容，还是很不划算。像标准编解码器（codecs）会把整帧画面重新编码，前景背景一起处理，把所有像素一视同仁，完全不管场景里有什么语义结构。结果就是带宽（bandwidth）浪费得很厉害，尤其当背景基本不动、真正在动的只有几个显眼主体（salient actors）的时候。我们提出 GenStream，一个语义流媒体框架（semantic streaming framework），用紧凑、结构化的元数据（metadata）取代密密麻麻的视频帧。它不是直接传像素，而是把每个场景编码成骨骼关键点（skeletal keypoints）、相机视角参数（camera viewpoint parameters）和静态 3D 背景模型（static 3D background model）的组合。这些信息传到客户端（client）后，由生成模型（generative model）重建出照片级逼真（photorealistic）的人体形象，再按原视角把它们合成进 3D 场景里。这套路子能实现极限压缩（extreme compression）：在连续数据流（continuous data stream）上，跟 HEVC 比，带宽能省下超过 99.9%。我们拿奥运会花样滑冰的素材对 GenStream 做了部分验证，也展示了它在极少数据下依然可能保持很高感知保真度（perceptual fidelity）的潜力。当然，我们也承认，这会把一大笔计算成本（computational costs）甩给客户端，泛化（generalization）上也有不少挑战。但 GenStream 还是在体积化虚拟人合成（volumetric avatar synthesis）、跨视角的标准 3D 演员融合（canonical 3D actor fusion across views）和个性化观看体验（personalized viewing experiences）上开了新方向，为后编解码器时代（post-codec era）里可扩展的智能流媒体（scalable, intelligent streaming）打下基础。

articles.title: Weakening Neurons: An Input-Output Functionality in Transformers with Outsize Influence
articles.zh: 弱化神经元：Transformer中影响力超常的输入-输出功能单元
articles.summary: 如果你在琢磨模型可解释性或做剪枝，这篇说的"少数神经元左右输出"会直接影响你的压缩方案
articles.author: Sebastian Gerstner, Hilal AlQuabeh 等
articles.body: We analyze the learned input-output behavior of GLU-based neurons in large language models (LLMs). We propose a simple analysis method: For each neuron, we compute the cosine similarities between its input (reading) and output (writing) weight vectors. In this scheme, a strong negative cosine similarity indicates the neuron weakens the direction it detects in the residual stream, so we call this a weakening neuron. This allows us to gain a number of novel insights. First, we show that nine different LLMs have similar patterns: weakening neurons appear mostly in late layers whereas their counterparts, (conditional) strengthening neurons, are frequent in early-middle layers. Second, we find that weakening neurons display surprising behavior: even though there are few, they activate often and have a large influence on model behavior. Third, weakening neurons have a strong effect on model output when gate values are negative -- which is surprising since negative gate values are not expected to encode functionality.
articles.bodyZh: 我们分析了大型语言模型（LLMs）里，基于 GLU（门控线性单元）的神经元在训练之后学到的“输入—输出”行为。我们提了个很简单的分析方法：对每个神经元，算一算它输入（reading，读入）权重向量和输出（writing，写出）权重向量之间的余弦相似度（cosine similarity）。按这个思路，如果余弦相似度是个很强的负值，就说明这个神经元会把它在残差流（residual stream）里检测到的那个方向削弱掉，所以我们管它叫“削弱神经元”（weakening neuron）。这样一来，我们就能挖出一些挺新的发现。第一，我们发现九个不同的大语言模型都有相似的规律：削弱神经元大多出现在靠后的层，而它们对应的（条件）增强神经元（(conditional) strengthening neuron）则常常出现在前中段的层里。第二，我们发现削弱神经元的表现很让人意外：虽然数量不多，但它们经常被激活，而且对模型行为影响很大。第三，当门控值（gate value）为负时，削弱神经元会对模型输出产生很强的影响——这挺让人吃惊，因为按理说，负的门控值不应该承载什么功能。

articles.title: PACT: Can Enterprise AI Assistants Be Trusted Under Pressure?
articles.zh: PACT：企业级AI助手在压力下还值得信任吗？
articles.summary: 如果你要给公司上企业AI助手，这篇测的是它在诱导和高压场景下会不会松口，可以当上线前的风险清单
articles.author: Mika Okamoto, Ansel Kaplan Erol
articles.body: As corporate AI adoption continues to grow, enterprise-grade LLM agents are being deployed into sensitive contexts such as hiring, healthcare, and finance. In these contexts, compliance with rules specified in an agent's system context is a first-order legal concern. Currently, no evaluation framework systematically measures which LLM models tend to violate compliance rules, especially under pressure from a persistent user, a hurried manager, or circumstances where violation is convenient or attractive. We introduce PACT (Pressure-Applied Compliance Testing), a benchmark for rule-following under pressure in AI agents assisting employees in daily tasks across twelve regulated enterprise domains and forty-eight scenarios, each set in a realistic multi-turn conversation. Each benchmark item pairs a standing rule against a rule-violating shortcut, and applies a battery of pressures across different wordings and system-prompt modes. We construct PACT component by component under strict LLM-as-judge auditing to ensure samples are unambiguous, ungameable, and realistic enough to avoid eliciting evaluation-aware behavior. We use PACT to profile LLM compliance across six complementary metrics that create a holistic picture of an AI assistant's robustness under pressure and throughout multi-turn conversations, its transparency, and ability to correctly discern where a rule applies. We aggregate this profile into PACTScore, a reliability-weighted compliance rate over all items and modes. Our results across 22 common LLM models spanning multiple providers and sizes show substantial variability in compliance across models and metric dimensions. Even the strongest assistants mis-apply a rule on 6 to 10% of items, and ordinary user pressure raises the violation rate by 65% on average. PACT highlights compliance risks in LLM assistants, motivating guardrails and careful model selection.
articles.bodyZh: 随着企业在 AI 上的采用越来越多，企业级大语言模型智能体（enterprise-grade LLM agents）正被派到招聘、医疗、金融这些敏感场景里干活。在这些场景中，能不能遵守智能体系统上下文（system context）里定下的规则，是头等法律大事。可现在，还没有哪个评估框架能系统地量出来：哪些大语言模型（LLM）更容易违反合规（compliance）规则，尤其是在一个不依不饶的用户施压、一个催得急的经理施压，或者违规既方便又有好处的时候。我们推出了 PACT（Pressure-Applied Compliance Testing），这是一个基准测试（benchmark），用来衡量 AI 智能体在帮员工处理日常工作、面对压力时到底守不守规则。它覆盖十二个受监管的企业领域、四十八个场景，每个场景都是一段贴近现实的多轮对话（multi-turn conversation）。每个基准题都会把一条长期有效的规则和一个违规捷径放在一起，然后用不同说法、不同系统提示模式（system-prompt modes）施加一连串压力。我们按照严格的“LLM 当裁判”（LLM-as-judge）审计方式，一个部件一个部件地搭建 PACT，确保样本不含糊、没法钻空子，也足够真实，不会把模型逼出“我知道自己在被评测”的行为。我们用 PACT，从六个互补的指标（metrics）来给 LLM 的合规表现画个像：它在压力下、在多轮对话里到底稳不稳，透不透明，以及能不能正确判断一条规则该用在哪里。我们把这些画像汇总成 PACTScore，一个对所有题目和模式算出来的、按可靠性加权的合规率（reliability-weighted compliance rate）。我们跑了 22 个常见 LLM 模型，覆盖多家厂商、不同规模，结果显示：不同模型、不同指标维度上的合规表现差别很大。就算是最强的助手，也会在 6% 到 10% 的题目上用错规则；而普通用户一施压，违规率平均会涨 65%。PACT 把 LLM 助手中的合规风险摆到了台面上，也提醒我们要上护栏（guardrails），并且认真挑模型。

articles.title: Online Robust Reinforcement Learning Through Monte-Carlo Planning
articles.zh: 基于蒙特卡洛规划的在线鲁棒强化学习
articles.summary: 如果你要把强化学习落到真实环境，这篇给的是环境有扰动时仍能在线学习的规划方法
articles.author: Tuan Dam, Kishan Panaganti 等
articles.body: Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) is a powerful framework for solving complex decision-making problems, yet it often relies on the assumption that the simulator and the real-world dynamics are identical. Although this assumption helps achieve the success of MCTS in games like Chess, Go, and Shogi, the real-world scenarios incur ambiguity due to their modeling mismatches in low-fidelity simulators. In this work, we present a new robust variant of MCTS that mitigates dynamical model ambiguities. Our algorithm addresses transition dynamics and reward distribution ambiguities to bridge the gap between simulation-based planning and real-world deployment. We incorporate a robust power mean backup operator and carefully designed exploration bonuses to ensure finite-sample convergence at every node in the search tree. We show that our algorithm achieves a convergence rate of $\mathcal{O}(n^{-1/2})$ for the value estimation at the root node, comparable to that of standard MCTS. Finally, we provide empirical evidence that our method achieves robust performance in planning problems even under significant ambiguity in the underlying reward distribution and transition dynamics.
articles.bodyZh: 蒙特卡洛树搜索（Monte Carlo Tree Search，简称MCTS）是个很强大的框架，能用来解决复杂的决策问题，但它通常有个前提：模拟器和真实世界的运行规律得一模一样。这个假设确实帮MCTS在国际象棋、围棋和将棋这些游戏里大获成功，可一到真实场景，因为低保真模拟器（low-fidelity simulator）里存在建模不匹配，事情就会变得含糊、充满不确定性。在这项工作里，我们提出了一种新的、更稳健的MCTS变体，专门用来缓解动态模型里的这种不确定性。我们的算法处理的是状态转移动态（transition dynamics）和奖励分布（reward distribution）上的不确定性，想把基于模拟的规划和真实世界部署之间的差距补上。我们引入了一个稳健的幂平均回溯算子（robust power mean backup operator），还精心设计了探索奖励（exploration bonuses），来保证搜索树里每个节点都能实现有限样本收敛（finite-sample convergence）。我们证明，这个算法在根节点（root node）做价值估计时，收敛速度能达到 \(\mathcal{O}(n^{-1/2})\)，和标准MCTS差不多。最后，我们还给出了实验证据，说明就算底层的奖励分布和状态转移动态存在很大的不确定性，我们的方法在规划问题里也能保持稳健的表现。
